text:
alex: CI on main turned red ~ 15m ago. Lots of failures in runtime/tests/quantized_simd_test.py and a couple in allocator tests. Error looks like SIMD mismatch after quantization pass.

maria: seen it, thanks. reran the pipeline once - still red :grimacing:

ci-bot: [auto] Pipeline rerun started for commit main@sha=0f9a3b7

alex: stack snippet:
```
E   AssertionError: outputs differ beyond tolerance
runtime/tests/quantized_simd_test.py:47: in test_simd_quant
    assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-3)
```

mina: hmm that test was flaky historically but not blowing up cluster-wide like this.

alex: last green was main@sha=0f8442c (yesterday). suspecting the simd kernel rewrite from PR #4981 merged this morning.

tj: can someone bisect? I can do it if we agree it's worth it.

alex: yes pls. bisect range: 0f8442c..0f9a3b7. use `git bisect run ./tools/test-bisect -- tests/runtime/quantized_simd_test.py`

tj: starting bisect on a runner now, will post first bad/last good.

ci-bot: [auto] Bisect job queued on runner ci-bisect-07

tj: bisect found first bad commit: 0f9a1a2 - "opt: simd lane reorder for quant kernels" (PR #4981). Reproducer: `pytest -k quantized_simd_test::test_simd_quant -q --disable-warnings`

alex: thanks. can we revert PR #4981 for a release patch? Who owns the PR?

mina: I'm the reviewer on that PR, pinging @sre-oncall for revert approval and quick patch deploy.

sre-oncall: acknowledge, will coordinate a revert and hotfix rollout. ETA ~30m. @maria please prepare patch with revert commit and changelog note.

maria: on it. creating revert PR now and will mark for priority merge.

alex: extra note — add the failing test output to the PR description and mark as regression from simd rewrite.

tj: once revert is merged I'll rerun full CI and monitor. if anyone needs logs or local repro steps ping me.

mina: cheers. thanks all for quick action :thumbsup:
